text:
Situation: Bupivacaine hydrochloride has been on the FDA shortage list since 2018-02-20 and remains Current as of 2026-10-21. Corvale East holds 4.6 days of 2.5 mg/mL 10 mL vials. Corvale Lakeside holds 19.7 days and can spare 19 vials. Corvale General holds 17–22 days across presentations. The rule‑ranked option is to transfer 19 vials from Corvale Lakeside to Corvale East, raising East to 6 days on hand.

Why (FDA record): FDA first posted the shortage on 2018-02-20; status is Current as of 2026-10-21. NDC 00409-1159-01 lists Hospira, Inc. at FEI 1925262. Inspection 976095 at that plant ended 2016-06-08 with OAI classification, 622 days before the shortage posting. A Warning Letter was issued to the same plant on 2017-02-14, 371 days before the posting. NDC 31722-275-32 lists Aspiro Pharma Limited at FEI 3014483338; its most recent inspection ended 2023-08-11 with VAI classification.

Our position: Internal transfer is the fastest way to protect Corvale East without new purchasing risk. Corvale Lakeside can spare 19 vials while retaining two weeks of supply. Corvale General has ample stock but transfer would require a larger move. Three alternate manufacturers are not on the FDA shortage list today; two lack identifiable plant information on their labels.

Recommended actions:
1. Approve transfer of 19 vials of 2.5 mg/mL 10 mL bupivacaine from Corvale Lakeside to Corvale East — Pharmacy Director must approve the transfer request.
2. If additional supply is needed, evaluate transfer from Corvale General — Pharmacy Director must approve the transfer request.
3. Qualify Meitheal Pharmaceuticals Inc. as a backup source — Buyer must approve purchase agreement.
4. Qualify Anthea Pharma Private Limited as a backup source — Buyer must approve purchase agreement.
5. Qualify B. Braun Medical Inc. as a backup source — Buyer must approve purchase agreement.

Not recommended: No clinical dosing changes or formulary substitutions at this time; those decisions rest with treating clinicians and the committee.
